title: Cross-jurisdictional federated survival analysis — FL + TEE + DP-C (S-01 pattern, EP-11)
description: A worked example demonstrating the stepwise-from-private construction methodology applied to a cross-jurisdictional cancer-research deployment. Inspired by the architectural pattern described in GDS (2025) for UK-US federated survival analysis. Patient-level data never leaves jurisdiction; aggregation runs in a hardware-isolated enclave in a third jurisdiction; central DP bounds the released hazard-ratio estimates.

jurisdictional_context.cross_border_mechanism: UK Information Commissioner's Office IDTA + US institutional DUA; HIPAA Business Associate Agreement for US-side participant institutions; HRA approval for UK-side data flow
jurisdictional_context.notes: Patient records never move out of jurisdiction. Only DP-bounded aggregates leave the enclave. The cross-border mechanism governs movement of attestation, parameter manifests, and the released model — not raw records.

pet_components.role: local data retention — UK NHS trust records and US academic-medical-centre records each remain in their owning institution
pet_components.parameter_notes: Survival-analysis (Cox PH) gradient aggregation. Heterogeneity across UK / US cohorts requires per-site convergence monitoring.

pet_components.role: hardware isolation of aggregation server hosted in UK cloud region — protects intermediate gradient state from cloud operator and cross-border observers

parameters.side_channel_mitigations: no hyperthreading on enclave vCPUs; memory encryption; attestation pinned per round

pet_components.parameter_notes: Enclave region chosen for proximity to UK controllers and to keep aggregation under UK supervisory jurisdiction.

pet_components.role: formal output disclosure bound on the released hazard-ratio estimates — noise calibrated to the sensitivity of the Cox PH log-likelihood
pet_components.parameter_notes: ε=2.0 chosen for cross-jurisdictional review acceptability. PRV accountant for tighter composition across 60 rounds vs RDP.

trust_model.summary: UK and US institutions are semi-trusted data holders bound by institutional agreements. Aggregation operator (UK cloud region) is honest-but-curious at host OS level; TEE isolates the aggregation. Released model and parameter manifests cross jurisdictions under IDTA/DUA; DP bounds individual-level leakage from the model.

threat_actors.capability: can observe network traffic, OS memory outside the enclave, attestation provisioning

threat_actors.actor: curious aggregation coordinator inside the enclave
threat_actors.capability: observes individual per-institution gradient updates before summation
threat_actors.mitigated_by: DP-C added at aggregation; TEE isolates the coordinator code
threat_actors.residual_risk: Coordinator still sees individual DP-noised updates before summation (no MPC layer). Upgrading to S-03 (FL + MPC + DP-C) would close this gap.

threat_actors.actor: external researcher receiving the published model and hazard ratios
threat_actors.capability: membership inference and reconstruction attacks against the released estimates and model coefficients
threat_actors.mitigated_by: DP-C bound (ε=2.0, δ=1e-6); cross-jurisdictional output review by both UK and US sponsors
threat_actors.residual_risk: ε=2.0 still permits some MIA signal on outlier records; per-record vulnerability sweep (Carlini et al. 2022) recommended before public release

threat_actors.actor: regulatory or supervisory authority in either jurisdiction requesting inspection
threat_actors.capability: may request access to attestation logs, parameter manifests, DPIA, audit trail
threat_actors.mitigated_by: All assurance artefacts retained and inspectable; IDTA documents cross-border transfer basis
threat_actors.residual_risk: Divergent regulator interpretation across jurisdictions remains a non-technical residual

out_of_scope_threats: Byzantine poisoning attacks from participating institutions
Compromise of UK or US sponsor institution at the data-controller level
Re-identification via genomic linkage (data scope excludes genomic variables)

required_artefacts.artefact: attestation report and enclave measurement (TEE layer)
required_artefacts.notes: Per-round attestation. Hash pinned at round start; mismatch aborts the round.

required_artefacts.artefact: privacy accountant and parameter manifest (DP-C layer)
required_artefacts.notes: PRV accountant; ε=2.0 budget tracked across all 60 rounds

required_artefacts.artefact: training protocol and aggregation specification (FL layer)
side-channel mitigation declaration for the aggregation enclave

required_artefacts.notes: Joint UK-US clearance for each release
To be commissioned before any wider release of the model. Follows the Carlini et al. (2022) worst-record methodology.

assurance_targets.maturity_justification: Repeatable; documented; full assurance artefact set; cross-jurisdictional sign-off complete. Stage 4 (audit-ready) blocked pending per-record MIA sweep evidence and external review of the cross-jurisdictional governance package.

governance_controls.access_control: Institutional DUAs (UK NHS, US AMC); IDTA for transfer of model and manifests; researcher accreditation under both UK and US regimes
governance_controls.change_control: Bilateral change-control board (UK + US sponsors); change to ε, clipping, or aggregation rule requires joint sign-off

frameworks_applied.notes: Outputs only; deployment is not a TRE — but Safe Outputs principles applied to the joint clearance process
BAA covers US side; HIPAA does not apply to UK side

applicable_regulations.gap_notes: Section 251 NHS Act 2006 not required — patients consented to research use

standards_alignment.notes: PRV accountant documented; parameter governance under bilateral review

tooling_candidates.name: Google dp_accounting
tooling_candidates.notes: PRV accountant used for tight composition tracking

residual_risks.risk: Coordinator inside the enclave still sees individual DP-noised updates before summation — TEE does not provide MPC-grade isolation of individual contributions
residual_risks.mitigation_path: Upgrade to S-03 (FL + MPC + DP-C) for cross-party blindness if coordinator trust is further constrained

residual_risks.risk: Per-record MIA vulnerability not yet measured; ε=2.0 may admit appreciable worst-record leakage on outliers
residual_risks.mitigation_path: Commission per-record vulnerability sweep (Carlini et al. 2022 methodology) before any wider release

residual_risks.risk: Divergent regulator interpretation of the cross-border mechanism between UK ICO and US HHS
residual_risks.mitigation_path: Bilateral sponsor governance maintains current alignment; documented cross-jurisdictional review minutes

utility_evidence.primary_metric: C-index (concordance) on the joint survival model
utility_evidence.notes: 5-point degradation at ε=2.0 vs non-private centralised baseline. Acceptable per bilateral clinical governance assessment for this exploratory phase.

stepwise_chain.name: Baseline — completely private
stepwise_chain.purpose: Starting state. UK NHS trust records and US AMC records sit in their owning institutions; no joint analysis possible. Patient-level information does not cross any boundary.
stepwise_chain.residual_risk: Trivially private. Joint cross-jurisdictional cancer survival analysis impossible — research question cannot be answered with single-jurisdiction cohort sizes.

stepwise_chain.name: Enable distributed computation
stepwise_chain.purpose: Allow each institution to compute Cox PH gradients on its own data without raw records leaving the jurisdiction.
stepwise_chain.assurance_anchor: training protocol specification; round-participation log; per-site convergence reports
stepwise_chain.residual_risk: Gradient inversion and participation-inference attacks against individual updates remain feasible; coordinator sees per-institution contributions.

stepwise_chain.name: Bound per-update and output leakage via central DP
stepwise_chain.purpose: Address EP-04 leakage from step 1; bound what the released hazard ratios and the final model reveal about any individual.
stepwise_chain.trust_assumption_added: trusted curator at the aggregation step; named composition theorem (PRV); parameter governance under bilateral sign-off
stepwise_chain.assurance_anchor: PRV accountant; parameter manifest (ε=2.0, δ=1e-6, Gaussian, clipping=0.5); composition assumption declaration across 60 rounds
stepwise_chain.residual_risk: Coordinator still sees individual DP-noised updates before summation; per-record vulnerability sweep not yet commissioned.

stepwise_chain.name: Protect the aggregation environment in a UK enclave
stepwise_chain.purpose: The aggregator runs on cloud infrastructure in the UK; protect data-in-use from the cloud operator and bind execution to UK supervisory jurisdiction.
stepwise_chain.trust_assumption_added: hardware-anchored trust (AWS Nitro attestation chain); regional pinning to eu-west-2
stepwise_chain.assurance_anchor: per-round attestation report; enclave measurement; side-channel mitigation declaration; regional pinning evidence
stepwise_chain.residual_risk: Hardware vendor compromise; side channels not covered by declared mitigations; enclave memory limits future model size.

stepwise_chain.name: Make the cross-jurisdictional context governable
stepwise_chain.purpose: Cross-border movement of attestation reports, parameter manifests, and the released model needs an explicit legal basis. Address EP-11 directly rather than treating it as implicit.
stepwise_chain.trust_assumption_added: institutional trust (UK ICO + US HHS) under documented cross-border mechanism
stepwise_chain.assurance_anchor: UK IDTA; US institutional DUA; HIPAA BAA for US side; HRA approval (UK) + IRB approval (US); joint output-clearance log; bilateral change-control board
stepwise_chain.residual_risk: Divergent regulator interpretation across jurisdictions remains a non-technical residual; future tightening of either regime may require renegotiation. The per-record MIA sweep is committed but not yet delivered — until then the worst-case disclosure for outlier patients is unmeasured.

change_log.change: Initial card created as worked example for the stepwise-from-private methodology in a cross-jurisdictional context. Inspired by the GDS (2025) UK-US federated survival analysis pilot architectural pattern.
change_log.author: Privacy Explorer

change_log.change: Migrated to schema 1.2: added risk_calibration block with μ-DP, attack target, and operational interpretation. Empirical worst-record TPR populated as a placeholder pending the privacy-eval per-record sweep.
change_log.author: Privacy Explorer

risk_calibration.operational_interpretation: Worst-record membership inference at FPR=0.001 is bounded at TPR ≤ ~0.025 under the declared composition assumption — roughly 25× the chance baseline. This is the operationally relevant statement for cross-jurisdictional review, alongside the raw ε=2.0 / δ=1e-6.
risk_calibration.notes: μ-DP derived from ε=2.0, δ=1e-6 via gdpnum at the FPR=0.001 operating point. Regret of 0.006 is within the Desfontaines-recommended ≤0.01 threshold, so μ-DP alone is a faithful summary at this operating point. Curve attached as defence-in-depth and to support stretch reviewers.
